candidates.title: PRT player process misses backlog inputs: epoch N+1's listener fetches InputAdded logs only from epoch N's seal block, so inputs left pending by the 2^24 per-epoch cap are never delivered and the player crash-loops
candidates.component: PRT player/bridge in doc/recipes: crisium.lua (epoch listener setup) + prt-epoch.lua (epoch listener)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support. No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI.'); it stands in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua:266-267 (first_input_block = previous_seal and previous_seal.log.blockNumber or first_block); doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua:38 (history:get_logs(address, self.first_input_block, ...)), :70-74 (index filter and 'input stream has a gap or duplicate' assert), :91-94 ('sealed input count mismatch' assert), :183 (first_input_block); referee side: cartesi-rollups/contracts/src/DaveConsensus.sol _nextInputIndexUpperBound (lowerBound + min(pending, MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH)) and acceptStagedTournamentResult ('seal at most one input span; the backlog waits for later epochs')
candidates.description: DaveConsensus seals epoch N with [lo_N, hi_N), hi_N = lo_N + min(getNumberOfInputs - lo_N, 2^24). When more than 2^24 inputs are pending at the seal, inputs hi_N, hi_N+1, ... were added to the InputBox BEFORE the seal block S_N, yet the referee assigns them to epoch N+1 (whose lower bound is hi_N). crisium.lua opens the listener for epoch N+1 with first_input_block = S_N (block of epoch N's EpochSealed log), with the comment 'An input logged in the previous seal's block can still belong to this epoch', and prt-epoch.lua fetches the application's InputAdded logs only from that block (prt-log-history fetches from first_blocks[address]). The backlog inputs (blocks < S_N) are never fetched. The epoch-N listener deliberately skipped them (index >= input_begin + MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH), as its header says ('an input ... past the epoch's input limit, belongs to a later player'), but the later player never sees them. Consequences: the first input fetched for epoch N+1 has index > input_begin + 0, so poll() raises 'input stream has a gap or duplicate'; if no input arrives after S_N, the EpochSealed of epoch N+1 (upper bound hi_N + k, k>0) hits 'sealed input count mismatch'. Either way the crisium process dies, prt-supervise.sh relaunches it, it rebuilds the listener with the same first_input_block and dies again: the honest player (and the sentinel, which uses the same code) never joins or defends epoch N+1 or any later epoch. The same happens after every capped seal, and also on relaunch, since the listener is rebuilt from the chain with the same first block.
candidates.trigger: Any input sender (untrusted, 'any bytes, any count'; section 7 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts') adds more than 2^24 inputs to the application while an epoch is open, so that more than 2^24 are pending when acceptStagedTournamentResult seals the next epoch (e.g. a contract looping InputBox.addInput; ~30k gas per input, ~5e11 gas total, cheap on an L2). No other precondition; ordinary chain operation, no reorg.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from the chain state alone: DaveConsensus explicitly supports the backlog (MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH comment 'excess inputs stay pending'; prt-lua-bridge.md: 'Its consensus seals at most 2^24 pending inputs per epoch and leaves the rest for later epochs'). The input box accepts unlimited inputs per application. Reproduced deterministically with a fake chain (see evidence) without needing 2^24 real inputs, since the listener only looks at log block numbers and InputBox indices.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No. The trigger is input senders sending many inputs, an adversary capability (section 7). It does not need a deployment to violate A1-A8 (DaveConsensus caps correctly), a reorg, a snapshot, an API caller, or an incorrectly designed application. The component is the Lua player/bridge in doc/recipes, not the sling node or the Cartesi Rollups Node, not prt-dishonest.lua, not a *-test file.

2. Role: AUDIT.md component table: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... | Support. No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI.' crisium.lua and prt-epoch.lua are the player process and its epoch listener (prt-lua-bridge.md lists both as bridge files). It stands in for the honest operator (section 3: 'implementations of an operator that no deployment runs').

3. High/Medium cases: section 3 Support: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator'. In the honest-operator role it would violate R4: 'The honest operator defends every epoch whose dispute is open ... It assigns inputs to epochs exactly as the referee does, including the input limit per epoch (A3).' and 'From any reachable state ... the honest operator can always compute the claim', at a reachable chain state, which section 8 rates Critical ('violating any rule or obligation at a reachable state, or anywhere on the honest operator's path, is critical'; also 'A crash ... caused by data from other parties that the honest operator must process' - the on-chain input record is data it must process, section 4). Hence Medium as a support defect.

4. Critical: not applicable to a support component (step 2: 'A defect that only a support component shows is never above Medium'). If triage judges that a production validator shares this epoch-assignment logic it would be Critical there, but the sling node / Rollups Node are out of scope.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness failure in the stand-in honest operator: after a flood of inputs, the honest player cannot compute or post its claim for the epoch that holds the backlog (and every later epoch), so if it is the only honest party, any claim, including a fabricated final state with fabricated outputs, wins those epochs unopposed. It also contradicts the recipe's own documented behavior (prt-epoch.lua header, prt-lua-bridge.md 'leaves the rest for later epochs').
candidates.evidence: Scratch script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/A3/backlog.lua drives the real prt-epoch.lua with a fake chain/ABI/player: epoch 0 sealed at block 100 with [0, 2^24), backlog input index 2^24 at block 50, another input 2^24+1 at block 120, epoch 1 listener with input_begin=2^24 and first_input_block=100 (as crisium computes). Output: 'first fetch block(s): 100,100', 'poll ok: false .../prt-epoch.lua:73: input stream has a gap or duplicate', nothing delivered (exit 1). Control (backlog-control.lua, first_input_block=1): both inputs delivered as offsets 0,1 (exit 0).
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua with harness.main: build an epoch listener via prt-epoch.new with a fake chain whose logs() honors fromBlock, a fake abi (event(log) returns a prebuilt event table, topics() returns {}) and a recording player; the previous seal is at block S with inputIndexUpperBound = lo + 2^24 and an InputAdded with index lo + 2^24 sits at a block < S; compute first_input_block exactly as crisium.lua does (ideally by factoring/reusing crisium's expression, or by running crisium against a minimal fake JSON-RPC). Assert (R4/A3) that poll() succeeds and the player receives input_added(0, ...) for the backlog input and input_added(1, ...) for the next one, and that an EpochSealed(N+1, lo+2^24, lo+2^24+2) is accepted. Exits 1 today ('input stream has a gap or duplicate'), 0 once the listener fetches from a block at or before the first input of its range (e.g. the consensus deployment block, or the block of input hi_N).

candidates.title: PRT referee model accepts an input record with more inputs than the per-epoch input limit (no count check in new_dapp_contract/run_epoch)
candidates.component: PRT referee model in doc/recipes: prt.lua new_dapp_contract / run_epoch / new_referee
candidates.role: Referee model (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT referee model in doc/recipes | Referee model')
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua:851-861 (new_dapp_contract: inputs = map(input_paths, fs.read_file), no bound), :806-811 (run_epoch announces every input and epoch_sealed(#inputs)), :3328 (inputs from the command line), :2211 (player asserts offset < 2^24)
candidates.description: A3 requires 'The input record assigns no more inputs to an epoch than the input limit per epoch.' The model's input record (dapp_contract.inputs) is taken verbatim from its input paths with no check against 2^ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH, whereas the deployed DaveConsensus caps each epoch at 2^24 and defers the rest. With more than 2^24 inputs, run_epoch announces offsets >= 2^24 that have no position in the dispute grid (mcycle tree height 24+48-p) and the honest player's add_pending_input asserts 'input offset past the epoch's input limit', so the honest player stops while the referee keeps running the tournament.
candidates.trigger: Whoever starts the model referee passes more than 2^24 input files (or calls the exported prt.new_dapp_contract with that many). Not an input sender: the model's input record is the referee operator's own argument list.
candidates.reachability: Practically unreachable through the CLI: 2^24 arguments need far more than Linux's argv limit (each argument costs at least its pointer plus a NUL; about 2 MiB of argv total by default). Reachable only through the Lua API (new_dapp_contract is exported), which is trusted in intent. No adversary-controlled input sequence reaches it.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Possibly: section 8 excludes 'Defects that need an untrusted party to call the machine API directly' and the trigger is the trusted operator of the model, not an input sender; section 4 treats the caller as trusted in intent. The section-3 rule for the referee model ('A defect in what it accepts or derives is rated as if a deployed referee had it') argues the other way.

2. Role: Referee model (AUDIT.md table). Section 3: 'a disagreement between the two on what a referee verifies or derives is a defect in one of them'; the manual's model of DaveConsensus caps epochs, the Lua model does not.
3. High/Medium: none of the listed cases matches directly.

4. Critical reading: as if a deployed referee accepted more than 2^24 inputs per epoch, it would violate A3 ('assigns no more inputs to an epoch than the input limit per epoch') and stop the honest operator (R4) - Critical. But there is no adversary trigger: the only way in is the model operator's own input list, which cannot exceed argv limits through the CLI.

5. Low reading: a real defect (missing A3 bound in the model) that no untrusted party can trigger: Low. Deciding fact: whether the model's input list counts as 'the on-chain input record' fillable by untrusted senders (then Critical) or as trusted operator configuration (then Low/out of scope). Hunter's estimate: Low.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Only through the model's fidelity: the model does not implement the A3 count bound that the deployed referee enforces, so it cannot stand in for the referee on input assignment at the limit. No goal break without a trusted operator supplying an over-limit input list.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only (prt.lua lines cited). Not run (2^24 inputs).
candidates.test_idea: Call prt.new_dapp_contract with an input_paths table of 2^24 + 1 entries pointing to one small file (or monkeypatch fs.read_file) and assert that it refuses (or that run_epoch announces at most 2^24 inputs and defers the rest). Exits 1 today because it accepts; 0 once bounded.

not_covered: Gas of the honest maximum-size delivery proof was not measured on chain. Measured instead: the honest delivery+step witness for the largest InputBox input (EvmAdvance of 65,508 bytes, INPUT_MAX_SIZE = 65,536) with the regenerated step's logs is 93,964 bytes (cmio log 8 accesses, step log 7), i.e. 94,180 bytes of winLeafMatch calldata (matches Dave's documented 'maximum input's 94,180 bytes'); a signed type-2 tx is about 94.3 KB, under geth/reth's 128 KiB txpool limit. Gas relied on Dave's Gas.WIN_LEAF_MATCH = 5,536,000 allocation, under the EIP-7825 2^24 per-tx cap (not independently measured). Chains with smaller tx-size limits (e.g. Arbitrum's sequencer max tx data size, believed to be 95,000 bytes) leave under 1 KB of margin; not verified.

prt-transactions.lua gas limit = min(max(2*estimate, 2*exhausted), block gas limit) caps at the block gas limit, not at the EIP-7825 per-transaction cap (2^24); an estimate above ~8.39M or an out-of-gas retry above it would sign an invalid tx. Not pursued: honest estimates appear well below that; no adversarial way found to force an out-of-gas retry.

DaveConsensus.provideMerkleRootOfInput reads the CURRENT sealed epoch's bounds, not those of the epoch of the calling tournament; a leaf match of an older epoch's inner tournament still callable after the next seal would verify against the newer epoch's inputs. Believed harmless (an older epoch's root is already settled before the next seal, so such a leaf result cannot change any settlement), but the Tournament finish/elimination rules that would confirm it (A1/A8 territory) were not checked.

Checked and found consistent (no candidate): input bytes bound by keccak to InputBox.getInputHash; input Merkle root height max(ceilLog2(len),5) equals SendCmioResponse/send_cmio_response write size (floor-log2 +1 rounding, min word size 5) and zero padding; request type hard-coded HTIF_YIELD_REASON_ADVANCE_STATE in CartesiStateTransition, prt.lua referee and player; MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH = 2^24 equals ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_ADVANCE_STATES_PER_EPOCH and 24+48+20 = 92 = height(0)+log2step(0); out-of-range input slot returns root 0 and forbids input bytes; InputBox inputs cannot exist before DaveConsensus deployment (app created in the same tx, ApplicationNotDeployed check); epoch-listener ordering of InputAdded vs EpochSealed within a block/tx; rollups-contracts CanonicalMachine constants from solidity-step 0.15.0 (TX buffer, iflags.Y, tohost addresses, log2 max outputs) equal the regenerated ones.
The Rust/sling node and Cartesi Rollups Node input assignment (out of scope) were not examined; whether a production validator shares the backlog defect of candidate 1 is unknown.
machine-guest-tools handling of maximum-size inputs (64 KiB) in the rx buffer was not examined (only that 64 KiB < 2 MiB rx buffer).
Behavior of the prt.lua referee model and players for inputs larger than the rx buffer (no-op delivery) was checked only by reading, not run.
Dave docs/reviews/* were deliberately not read (possible earlier-review material).
